claims.text: A calibrated hybrid Monte Carlo/molecular dynamics framework combined with virtual and targeted experimental DSC can predict HEA melting properties.
The proposed method can predict melting temperature, enthalpy of fusion, entropy of fusion, and volume change at melting to approximately ±10% of experiment.
The approximately ±10% performance is expected across a diverse set of high-entropy alloys.
Equilibrium solid-state configurations benchmarked against crystallographic and thermodynamic data are suitable initial models for melting simulations.
Simulations spanning 800 °C to 1500 °C cover the relevant melting regime for the proposed HEA systems.
Using sufficiently large simulation systems enables liquid-nucleation events to be captured.
Calibration of interatomic potentials over a broad HEA composition space improves the reliability of melting predictions.
High-purity inert DSC conditions minimize extraneous effects in experimental melting measurements.
Simulated atomic-level energy fluctuations and disorder parameters correlate with DSC signals representing latent heat and other fusion characteristics.
Calibrated interatomic potentials reproduce HEA melting by capturing progressive structural and energetic transitions.
Hybrid MC/MD thermodynamic profiles provide melting temperature, fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, and melting volume change.
Agreement between simulated and experimental DSC data would establish the reliability of the model.
A discrepancy greater than 10% in melting temperature or latent heat would invalidate the simulation method for reliable HEA melting prediction.
Existing DSC data and preliminary simulations on simpler HEA systems provide a baseline for evaluating the approach.
The approach is most applicable to HEAs analogous to equiatomic CoCrCu systems.
HEAs with substantially different elemental compositions or complex phase equilibria may require additional potential calibration.
Prediction accuracy depends on the quality of interatomic-potential calibration across HEA compositions.
A DSC peak position can be used to determine melting temperature.
The area under a DSC peak can be used to determine latent heat.
Changing heating and cooling rates should generate DSC trends that the simulation can reproduce.

contradictions.description: The headline claim presents approximately ±10% accuracy across a diverse HEA set, whereas the boundary restricts best applicability to CoCrCu-analogous systems and the uncertainty field says broader-composition validation remains necessary.
